newValue.overview: Design plan for "E2E Flow 2026-06-15 1029". This application aims to Verify the full create-plan-roadmap-run lifecycle from the UI and persist the resulting state correctly.. It must satisfy 3 key requirements and serve QA and product owners. The design breaks down the application into modular components with clear responsibilities and communication patterns.
newValue.architecture: Layered architecture with 3 primary components: API Gateway, Persistence Layer, Validation Service. Component communication via well-defined interfaces. Persistence abstracted through repository pattern. Cross-cutting concerns (logging, validation, error handling) centralized. Constraints: No external credentials, Must complete entirely in local dev mode.

components.name: API Gateway
components.description: HTTP API entry point with request validation and routing
components.responsibility: Accept and route HTTP requests, validate schemas, return responses

components.name: Persistence Layer
components.responsibility: Create, read, update, delete operations with transactional consistency

components.name: Validation Service
components.description: JSON Schema validation and type checking
components.responsibility: Ensure all data matches defined schemas before persistence

tradeoffs: Monolithic architecture prioritizes simplicity and startup speed over horizontal scalability. Recommend microservices if request volume exceeds 10K/min.
File-based persistence chosen for initial phases for simplicity. Plan migration to database (PostgreSQL/MongoDB) before production at scale.
Synchronous request handling keeps code simple but may impact latency under high concurrency. Consider async job queues (Bull/RabbitMQ) for long-running ops.
Single-threaded event loop suitable for I/O-bound operations. Consider clustering for CPU-bound workloads.
recommendations: Implement structured logging from the start (Winston/Pino) with correlation IDs for tracing.
Set up health checks and graceful shutdown handlers before deploying to production.
Establish error handling standards and failure recovery patterns early.
